story.head: Stay out of the box, Sharks
paras: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Sharks (12-14-2) beat Vegas 4-1 on Friday. Going in, the Sharks are third in the Pacific (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Rangers fourth in the Metropolitan (18th).

The Sharks’ record (.464) is about what their chances are worth. The Rangers have played better than their record (.540) says: their chances are worth about .612, and their finishing has held them back.

The Sharks ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also have a leaky penalty kill (31st), so the Rangers’ power play (8th) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. San Jose has scored 2.57 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. As for the Rangers, they get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (2nd). Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Macklin Celebrini (11 G / 22 A / 33 P in 26 GP) leads the Sharks in scoring. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (2 G / 26 A / 28 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in five straight games against San Jose. Alexis Lafrenière (10 G / 12 A / 22 P in 25 GP) has a team-high ten goals.

San Jose has two options in net: Yaroslav Askarov (7-10-1 / .893 SV% in 18 GS) and Alex Nedeljkovic (5-4-1 / .888 SV% in 10 GS). Askarov has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. the Rangers also has two options: Dylan Garand (7-9-1 / .907 SV% in 15 GS) and Joonas Korpisalo (3-1-0 / .912 SV% in 4 GS). Garand has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
